Exact backup lifetimes, control-record durability/compaction, mandatory financial/security retention and provider deletion timelines remain explicit prelaunch decisions with the operations and launch-markets tickets. This contract sets their required behavior without inventing jurisdiction-specific duties or accepting indefinite retention. They must validate the seven-day active-deletion target and 24-hour export expiry against provider behavior and the accepted budget, or return an explicit proposed change.

### Purchases and providers

An existing account's purchase cannot be attached to another account. Show the conflict and offer sign-in/recovery without exposing the other account's identity. A deliberate deletion is the accepted exception: after verified store restoration and explicit confirmation, a still-valid subscription may attach to a new account. Atomically serialize ownership so concurrent restoration cannot grant multiple accounts the same purchase. Delayed webhooks and old-account tokens cannot reverse the accepted transfer. No private data, public identity, previous allowance balance or cached premium proof transfers.

Deleting the app account is not a claim that the store subscription was cancelled or refunded. Explain billing and provide store management access before deletion; do not block immediate deletion until the paid period ends. Subscription verification owns provider selection, entitlement timelines, proof requirements and transaction-retention details, consuming this ownership contract. Restoration is never manual recovery of an old private account.

Qualify Apple/Google native and browser flows on iOS and Android, verified linking/unlinking and email changes, relay delivery, deep links, revocation and deletion. Configure production email delivery and abuse limits; Supabase's development mail service is not an assumed launch service. Do not log email codes or provider tokens. Provider secret rotation, Apple notification handling and deletion token revocation require explicit operational ownership and monitoring. Missing provider capabilities are implementation gates, not permission to silently remove an accepted sign-in method.

### Required implementation scenarios

These are acceptance requirements, not tests run during this planning session.

| Scenario | Required outcome |
| --- | --- |
| Apple relay sign-in, then Google with a different email | Explicit linking into the signed-in account preserves one owner; an already-owned identity gives a conflict without merging. |
| Same verified email through supported providers | Provider-verified identity behavior returns the intended account; no application email-string merge. |
| Email sign-in for an unknown address; failed email change or unlink | No accidental recovery claim; no silent new account on email sign-in; at least one usable method survives changes. |
| Offline sign-out, then another account signs in | Original records/key remain isolated and need fresh online sign-in; no data or allowance inheritance. |
| Expired token or provider outage versus confirmed revocation | Outage preserves permitted cached access; confirmed revocation locks; neither erases private data. |
| Revoked JWT used against API, storage, exports or direct database access | Live account/session authorization denies new access despite unexpired JWT. |
| Export with failed uploads and records on another offline device | Server snapshot and labelled local supplement remain distinct; unknown remote-local records are explicitly excluded. |
| Deletion accepted but response lost; uploads/jobs arrive concurrently | One irreversible acceptance; status retry is safe; no restored account or renewed public contribution. |
| Deletion worker fails after public removal | Account stays inaccessible, cleanup retries and completion remains pending. |
| Old device reconnects; old email creates a new account | Confirmed deletion wipes only the old local account; new ID cannot inherit old records or receipts. |
| Restore a backup from before deletion or sharing withdrawal | Control state is reconciled before service/public access resumes; no resurrection. |
| Deleted author has saved copies and remixes elsewhere | Executable/history references survive under accepted rights; controlled attribution/prose disappears. |
| Restore subscription owned by active versus deliberately deleted account | Active owner requires sign-in; deleted owner permits verified explicit benefit-only restoration, serialized against competing restores. |

### Named handoffs

- [Subscription verification and entitlement implementation](https://github.com/0xRowdy/true-count/issues/23): implement existing-owner conflicts, deliberate-deletion restoration, store proof and serialized ownership, billing cancellation guidance, provider reconciliation and limited transaction retention.
- [Launch markets and data residency](https://github.com/0xRowdy/true-count/issues/27): resolve applicable export/deletion duties, required retention, mail/auth/provider processing regions, and any shorter legal deletion periods. Store documentation alone does not settle these legal requirements.
- [Backend operating envelope and disaster recovery](https://github.com/0xRowdy/true-count/issues/28): select finite backup/processing/control-record retention, independent deletion-control protection, restoration reconciliation, email/provider operating costs and monitoring; verify the accepted processing targets within budget or propose an explicit change.
- [Community content rights and author deletion](https://github.com/0xRowdy/true-count/issues/29): resolve publication/copy/remix permissions, attribution and author-erasure obligations, including independently copied text and required exceptions to retained executable copies; wait for launch-market inputs. This graduated from release-readiness fog and does not reopen the accepted baseline without an explicit decision.
- Broader release readiness: account-required app-review rationale, final privacy/deletion disclosures, built-in/reference content licensing, and age/content requirements remain on the map. These are not certified by this decision.

No production authentication, export service, deletion job, store integration or restore procedure is implemented here. Preserve the three-game launch scope and the user's direction to avoid elaborate offline account-lifecycle flows.

22.title: Authentication and account lifecycle

23.body:
## Question

Which store/provider integration and account-level entitlement service should implement premium across iOS and Android?

Map purchase, restoration, renewal, cancellation, store billing grace, expiration, billing recovery/account hold, refunds/revocation, duplicate subscriptions and cross-account purchase cases into the accepted lifecycle. Wait also for Authentication and account lifecycle to establish identity/linking contracts.

Use store-recognized entitlement state and its applicable end, including billing grace, independently of True Count's offline deadline: min(successful verification + seven days, recognized entitlement end + 72 hours). A confirmed entitled subscriber must not be denied because the paid period ended. Define handling of responses with no usable entitlement end, successful negative verification, failed verification, cross-platform benefits and trusted elapsed time.

Choose integration/provider, store configuration, operational notification/reconciliation and recovery behavior. Define acceptance checks for outages, clock uncertainty, store grace, restore/account conflicts, and upgrade/downgrade during active training-bankroll play; keep entitlement enforcement separate from engine execution. Verify current primary-source store requirements rather than assuming a provider satisfies them.

Use the accepted [Offline access and subscription lifecycle](https://github.com/0xRowdy/true-count/issues/8) as the product contract. Wait for [Mobile platform and shared game-engine architecture](https://github.com/0xRowdy/true-count/issues/16) before choosing the implementation. This ticket resolves a planning decision, not production implementation. Preserve the three-game launch scope and account isolation/recovery correctness. Proposed scope reductions remain unaccepted and require explicit agreement.

comments.body:
[Local persistence and account synchronization architecture](https://github.com/0xRowdy/true-count/issues/21#issuecomment-5565344184) is resolved. Use the selected Supabase account-state transaction/receipt boundary and stable account IDs after the authentication decision. External store/provider calls stay outside the database transaction; verified results enter through a dedicated authorized operation. A trusted server-time anchor alone does not verify subscription state or issue allowance. Preserve the original offline deadline on verification failure, the recognized entitlement/grace rules, and the existing no-usable-end case.

The accepted native clock plan uses sleep-inclusive elapsed time with qualified boot continuity; uncertainty requires revalidation while permitted completion/settlement/history remain available. Confirmed upgrade/downgrade must preserve old-grant settlement and never duplicate daily allowance. Coordinate authoritative entitlement reconstruction after restore with [Backend operating envelope and disaster recovery](https://github.com/0xRowdy/true-count/issues/28). This handoff does not choose a billing provider or resolve this ticket.

[Authentication and account lifecycle](https://github.com/0xRowdy/true-count/issues/22#issuecomment-5565609337) is resolved through the live Q1–Q13 review. This is an accepted planning contract, not implemented software.

Use stable account IDs with Apple, Google and email-code sign-in; verified matching-email provider identities may link automatically, different-email linking is explicit, and existing accounts are never merged. Premium remains separate from sign-in and local content readiness.

A purchase attached to an existing account is nontransferable: require sign-in to its owner without disclosing that account's identity. Deliberate account deletion is the accepted exception: explicit online store-verified restoration may attach a still-valid subscription to a new account, transferring benefits only, never private records/profile/allowance balance. Resolve store proof, atomic single-owner reassignment, concurrent restores and delayed webhooks. A receipt cannot authorize support recovery of private data.

Deletion blocks account access immediately but does not claim cancellation/refund of store billing. Provide subscription-management guidance without requiring cancellation or paid-period expiry before deletion. Specify the minimal transaction/ownership retention needed for this restoration and coordinate legally required retention with launch markets and operations. Preserve the accepted offline entitlement deadlines and access boundaries. This handoff does not resolve subscription verification.

# Subscription verification and entitlement implementation — accepted decision

Decision ticket: [Subscription verification and entitlement implementation](https://github.com/0xRowdy/true-count/issues/23), part of the [MVP decision map](https://github.com/0xRowdy/true-count/issues/1).

Accepted through the live Q1–Q8 review, including the integrated design, supplemental current-store verification, operational targets and handoffs. This is planning, not production implementation. Preserve the accepted offline-access, authentication/account-lifecycle, and local-persistence decisions.

## Accepted choices

- **Q1 — Duplicate subscriptions:** prevent starting a second subscription in the app when the account already has premium through either store. Direct the player to manage the existing subscription. If overlapping subscriptions nevertheless occur, provide one premium entitlement, explain the duplicate billing, and offer both store-management links. Do not add subscription durations together.
- **Q2 — Billing channels:** use Apple and Google in-app subscriptions only at launch. Retain the accepted monthly and annual plans and account-level premium across platforms. Web subscription checkout is outside MVP; the accepted minimal web account-deletion path remains in scope.
- **Q3 — Provider:** use RevenueCat for store integration, with True Count's backend controlling purchase ownership and premium access. Disable automatic purchase transfers and qualify the deliberate-deletion restoration exception during implementation; provider defaults alone do not satisfy account ownership. If qualification fails, reopen the integration design rather than weaken the accepted lifecycle.
- **Q4 — Billing grace:** configure 16 days on Apple and 7 days on Google. Store billing grace remains distinct from True Count's accepted offline verification deadline.
- **Q5 — Subscription pause:** disable Google's optional subscription pause feature at launch. Cancellation of renewal preserves access through the recognized entitlement end; a player may subscribe again later.
- **Q6 — Billing-cadence changes:** monthly-to-annual and annual-to-monthly changes begin at the next renewal, with uninterrupted premium and no immediate replacement charge.
- **Q7 — Family Sharing:** launch premium covers the purchasing True Count account only. Apple Family Sharing remains disabled. The account's benefits still work across its iOS and Android devices.

- **Q8 — Integrated design:** accepted the complete design below, including direct Apple/Google checks for verification freshness, pending-purchase recovery, single-owner restoration, reconciliation cadences, operational targets, release qualification and the existing retention/recovery handoffs.

## Integrated design — accepted in Q8

The following makes Q1–Q7 and the previously accepted contracts concrete and was accepted in Q8. All verification scenarios below are requirements for future implementation, not tests claimed to have run.

### Store and provider configuration

Use `react-native-purchases` in Expo development/production builds and one RevenueCat project containing the iOS and Android apps. Map all launch products to one premium entitlement. Keep production and sandbox credentials, evidence and access isolated; sandbox purchases cannot grant production premium. Native module/SDK versions must meet the stores' submission requirements at release and pass the matrix selected by [Mobile device support and accessibility](https://github.com/0xRowdy/true-count/issues/25); that decision remains open.

On Apple, place monthly and annual auto-renewable products in one subscription group at the same service level. Enable 16-day billing grace for paid-to-paid renewals, test in sandbox, then enable production. Keep Family Sharing disabled. On Google, use separate monthly and annual subscription products, each with its corresponding auto-renewing base plan, both mapped to the same premium entitlement. This permits explicit `DEFERRED` product replacement in both directions without relying on same-subscription base-plan replacement modes. Include the current product/token in the replacement operation, process/acknowledge the new token when issued, and retain the current entitlement until its scheduled replacement. Configure required Google server notifications for RevenueCat's deferred handling.

Google grace is 7 days on both plans; retain automatic account-hold calculation, currently 60 days minus grace (53 days with this setting). Account hold does not grant premium. Pause stays disabled. Do not offer prepaid, installment, add-on, promotional or win-back products at launch; the accepted free training allowance supplies the preview. Re-enabling renewal of an existing subscription is management of that subscription, not a duplicate purchase. Retain and reconcile supported store-initiated renewals/resubscriptions rather than assuming every transaction started in the app.

Display the store-returned localized total recurring price and billing period, renewal terms, cancellation guidance, links to terms/privacy, Restore purchases and Manage subscription. The accepted provisional US prices remain $5.99/month and $39.99/year with identical benefits and no introductory premium trial. Localized prices and sale regions remain with launch-market planning. The annual total is prominent; a monthly equivalent cannot replace it. State the accepted periodic-verification condition for offline premium. Use original-store management links even on the other platform; overlapping subscriptions need both links rather than RevenueCat's single preferred management URL. Refund requests use the original store's supported process, without promising approval or silently canceling/refunding a purchase.

### Ownership and purchase flow

Use the signed-in account's stable, opaque identifier for RevenueCat; never email or display name. Configure the SDK only for the intended account before purchase/restore, prevent anonymous purchasing, and discard callbacks from an older account-session generation. RevenueCat customer identifiers and client-reported CustomerInfo are not authentication or independent authorization to premium.

The Supabase-backed subscription service owns the mapping from verified store purchase lineage to exactly one True Count account. Distinguish the store subscription and its replacement/renewal transactions from the premium access it contributes. Validate application/product, production versus sandbox, purchase authenticity, and existing ownership before accepting an update. Apple original transaction lineage and Google's linked purchase tokens must survive plan changes without producing a second owner. Store/provider calls happen outside database transactions; the final authorized transaction checks current account/deletion state, ownership generation and operation identity before updating entitlement state and the account synchronization feed.

Preflight purchases online against the account's existing subscriptions. Existing premium directs the player to manage its billing source; an intended same-store plan replacement is distinct from buying a second subscription. Concurrent store operations or purchases outside the app can still create overlaps, so do not promise global prevention. Retain each verified subscription independently and grant one premium benefit while any owned source qualifies; ending one source cannot revoke another valid source or add their durations together.

Bind purchase/restore retries to the original operation and store transaction. A canceled purchase does not change access. A pending store payment does not grant premium. A completed store charge awaiting backend acceptance shows verification pending with retry/restore and support options; do not initiate another charge to resolve it. A failed verification preserves only existing permitted access. Finish/acknowledge store transactions through the supported integration and durably track unresolved delivery; meet Google's acknowledgment deadline and verify this behavior when the application/backend fails. A verification receipt is not a second allowance grant.

### Restoration and deletion

Restoring on another device for the same account verifies the original store purchase and reuses its existing ownership. Cross-platform benefits then follow the True Count account; access on Android does not itself prove ownership of an Apple purchase. Explicit store restoration requires a supported device/store session capable of presenting that purchase. Explain the needed original-store access if the current platform cannot supply it.

If the purchase belongs to an existing account, require sign-in to that owner without revealing its identity. Account recovery continues to require a linked sign-in method. Support cannot turn a receipt into access to private records or a discretionary purchase transfer.

After deliberate account deletion only, an explicit online restoration request may reassign the verified subscription's benefits to a new authenticated account. Serialize restoration against deletion and competing restores using the purchase ownership record and its generation. Only one new owner wins; retries return the same accepted result. A delayed webhook is evidence about billing, never authority to reassign ownership or recreate a deleted account. No history, profile, allowance balance, or device-local activity transfers.

RevenueCat's keep-original-owner setting is the baseline. Its privileged transfer operation is broader than a single transaction; do not use it blindly when several subscriptions/apps could be affected. Reconcile provider identity through a scoped durable operation, preserving the backend ownership barrier throughout partial failure. Deleting a RevenueCat customer neither cancels store billing nor authorizes a new owner. The transfer API is documented between existing provider customers; do not assume it works with a deleted customer. If that customer is gone, first re-ingest the verified store evidence under a controlled billing identity, then reconcile the accepted ownership. Keep the reassignment operation pending until the necessary provider steps and final ownership acceptance succeed; cached SDK status never bypasses that barrier.

Restoration proof consists of evidence obtained through the original store restore flow, authenticated True Count intent and current server-side validation of that purchase lineage. A RevenueCat customer ID, order-number screenshot or support claim is insufficient. Receipts and purchase tokens are sensitive replayable evidence, not a cryptographic guarantee that a person just authenticated in store UI. Bind their submission to the requesting account/operation; enforce single ownership even on replay. Protect raw evidence in transport, storage and access paths, and never expose it in analytics or public profiles. Sandbox qualification must verify supported evidence extraction from the selected SDK/native adapter, deletion/re-ingestion, purchases on an Apple receipt with another account's history, competing restores and delayed events. If this cannot meet the accepted store-verified restoration contract, reopen the integration; do not silently substitute broad automatic transfers or support-based recovery.

### Entitlement normalization and delivery

Keep recognized store access separate from renewal intent, paid-period end, store grace end, offline deadline and verification failure. Active and store-grace states grant access. Cancellation of renewal alone preserves it. Confirmed expiration, revocation or account hold removes that source's access; a refund event must be interpreted according to its actual entitlement effect rather than assumed to revoke everything. Recovery restores only the verified source and owner. Unexpected/contradictory states require reconciliation and cannot manufacture a new offline window.

For confirmed current entitlement with usable end E, preserve the accepted deadline min(V + seven days, E + 72 hours), where V is a successful authoritative verification time. Use the recognized grace end when applicable, not stale paid expiry. A confirmed entitled response without usable E preserves current verified access and any valid previous offline deadline, but issues no new offline extension. Successful negative verification overrides previous grace for that source; failed verification leaves its original deadline unchanged. Aggregate overlapping sources without mixing one source's verification time with another's end.

**Accepted freshness strategy:** retain RevenueCat for purchase handling and lifecycle processing, and use supplemental server-to-store checks to establish V. Apple Get All Subscription Statuses and Google `purchases.subscriptionsv2.get` provide current subscription state. This needs server credentials plus verified Apple transaction lineage / Google purchase tokens; an authenticated server operation must retain these securely when purchasing/restoring, with a qualified native adapter if the selected RevenueCat SDK does not expose the needed evidence. A platform without local store proof can refresh an already-owned subscription through the evidence held by our backend.

RevenueCat's `request_date` is the request date, not a documented last-store-check timestamp. A successful RevenueCat GET, authentic SDK response, temporary provider entitlement, SDK offline grant, duplicate webhook or read of our saved snapshot cannot advance V. Store a separate observation time for such responses. Successful direct verification records the check's conservative server time (request start, accounting for delayed responses), evidence identity, source state, ownership generation and recognized E atomically. Serializing checks per lineage and rejecting stale generations prevents an older response from undoing a newer accepted check or reassignment. A failed direct check preserves prior V and its deadline; it is not successful negative verification. A recognized negative direct response supersedes that source's cached access immediately. A verified store event establishing revocation is also applied without waiting for a failed follow-up refresh; generic provider event labels alone do not establish this effect.

Use Apple's signed renewal grace expiry for an entitled grace state and Google's current entitled line item's expiry, including its dynamically extended grace. Check RevenueCat's explicit V1 `grace_period_expires_date` and V2 `gives_access`/active-entitlement `expires_at` against store fixtures; do not assume billing-period fields include grace or add the configured grace duration to a paid expiry. A pending Google replacement line item with no expiry must not obscure the currently active line item's end. Store-current evidence takes precedence over older provider observations; unexplained disagreements trigger reconciliation and an alert, not an arbitrary extra grace period.

Reading our saved snapshot or receiving a fresh server-time anchor must never advance V. Native elapsed time and boot-continuity checks follow the accepted persistence design. Clock uncertainty requires revalidation of time-limited rights while permitted settlement/history remain available. For the exceptional confirmed-entitled/no-usable-E case, current verified access authorizes the current connected foreground activity; pause/background, connectivity loss or failed required revalidation returns to any still-valid prior offline deadline. Recheck that exceptional state on the connected 60-second cadence. Do not invent a permanent right or reject the currently confirmed entitled response using a stale paid expiry.

Commit entitlement changes through the account-state synchronization boundary. Notify connected devices with a change hint and fetch authoritative state on foreground/reconnection and the accepted 60-second connected cadence. Do not call stores per game turn. The engine receives allowed execution boundaries from the application access layer; it does not import the billing SDK.

Preserve the accepted access-loss rules: finish the current turn, settle outstanding commitments, save, and stop new interactive turns; already-started challenges may finish under their existing exception. A verified upgrade stops further allowance consumption. A free training-bankroll session finishes its current turn and final settlement before new premium practice starts with ordinary funding. Old-grant settlement never refills a new grant. Downgrade uses only a still-valid available free allowance or an authorized new daily grant.

### Notifications, reconciliation and outages

Connect App Store Server Notifications V2 and Google RTDN to the supported RevenueCat integration. Authenticate RevenueCat webhooks with a configured server secret, validate environment/app/product, durably enqueue before acknowledgement, and deduplicate event IDs. Event names such as cancellation, billing issue and product change are triggers to reconcile current state; they are not interchangeable with expiration. Provider transfers never override our ownership table. Missing event delivery is handled by scheduled reconciliation; provider retries alone are insufficient.

Accepted launch cadence: perform a current-store check on purchase/restore acceptance, explicit Recheck access, a relevant lifecycle event, and crossing a known entitlement boundary. On app foreground/reconnection, refresh when the last check is at least six hours old; coalesce concurrent requests per purchase lineage. Ordinary 60-second account synchronization distributes existing authoritative state without polling stores per device every minute. Reconcile all known active/grace/retrying/held subscriptions at least daily, scheduling known renewal/grace boundaries separately and retaining a bounded retry queue for failures. Terminal subscriptions leave routine polling after pending events/recovery work is reconciled; later restore or store events can revalidate them.

The six-hour/daily cadences are operational defaults, not extra offline grace or guarantees of instant discovery. Every successful check may supply a new fixed offline deadline, delivered with its original V; downloading it later cannot move that time. After a current-store check fails, show stale/pending verification while preserving the prior deadline. Retry transient errors with jittered exponential backoff capped at five minutes, respect rate limits, and retain durable retry state. Bound/coalesce explicit rechecks to prevent retry storms without interpreting throttling as non-entitlement.

For online-only premium actions such as publication/rating, the account service authorizes from its accepted recognized entitlement and revalidates stale/expired evidence before allowing a new action. Client offline grace is not authority to write public contributions. A provider/store outage does not erase local records, revoke a still-valid cached offline grant, block permitted settlement, or grant extra allowance. A missing end, malformed response or ambiguous identity remains distinguishable from confirmed expiration. A completed charge awaiting verification stays pending; the app offers retry/restore and original-store support without another purchase prompt.

Accepted internal targets: begin processing accepted webhook work within one minute and alert if unprocessed work exceeds five minutes; propagate an accepted entitlement change to a healthy connected foreground client by its next 60-second account reconciliation. These are implementation targets, not store-delivery guarantees. Track verification failures/age, unacknowledged Google purchases, pending paid activation/restore, provider ownership mismatches, queue lag and reconciliation coverage through the accepted PostHog operational setup. Alert on Google acknowledgement still pending after one hour so recovery can occur before its three-day deadline. Keep access controls, secrets and sensitive tokens out of analytics.

### Retention and recovery handoffs

Retain the minimum protected purchase lineage, current owner/ownership generation, deletion marker and idempotent restore outcome necessary to prevent reassignment to an existing owner or revival of a deleted account. Retain raw tokens only as needed for verification/recovery, encrypted with restricted server access. Do not retain private gameplay, email or author profile as purchase-ownership evidence. Provider customer deletion and retained billing metadata must follow the accepted account-deletion target and the explicit limited-retention exceptions; this design does not authorize indefinite RevenueCat customer/history retention.

[Launch markets and data residency](https://github.com/0xRowdy/true-count/issues/27) must cover RevenueCat/store processing locations, disclosures, applicable billing/privacy obligations and any legally required transaction retention. [Backend operating envelope and disaster recovery](https://github.com/0xRowdy/true-count/issues/28) must settle finite billing/control/evidence retention, provider deletion processing, credential rotation, direct-store verification volume and cost, alert ownership, and restore drills. Include RevenueCat's currently published 1% tracked-revenue charge after its $2,500 monthly threshold, plus the direct-check workload; no provider-specific SLA is assumed.

After a backend restore, keep new premium acceptance and ownership changes behind recovery reconciliation. Restore protected deletion/ownership control state before accepting stale devices or store events; reconstruct current billing from stores and reconcile RevenueCat before issuing new entitlement snapshots. Never reconstruct V from the time a backup was loaded. Existing device offline deadlines remain unchanged while recovery is pending. The operations ticket must test loss of recent restore/deletion receipts and recover the authoritative single-owner result without reviving accounts or duplicating allowance.

### Required scenario acceptance

| Scenario | Required outcome |
| --- | --- |
| Purchase succeeds; backend response is lost or app closes | Same transaction resumes verification, one owner/access update, no second charge; acknowledgement/delivery recovery is monitored. |
| Pending payment, canceled checkout, temporary RevenueCat grant | No invented store-confirmed premium or V; current permitted rights remain. |
| Repeated cached RevenueCat GETs over more than seven days | V does not slide; only a successful qualified current-store check can refresh it. |
| Paid expiry precedes a currently entitled store-grace end | Premium remains; use the recognized grace end in the offline formula. |
| Confirmed entitled with missing/unusable E | Current verified access remains; no manufactured offline extension or stale-paid-end rejection. |
| Failed verification versus confirmed expiration/hold/revocation | Failure preserves prior deadline; a confirmed loss removes that source even before the deadline. |
| Cancellation or refund without loss of entitlement | Apply actual current access state, not a generic cancellation/refund label. |
| Recovery after grace or account hold | Restore the verified entitlement once, without allowance refill or private-account transfer. |
| Monthly/annual switch, new token now and future line item without expiry | No charge before agreed renewal; retain current access, acknowledge correctly, and preserve one lineage/owner. |
| Two subscriptions overlap; one later expires/refunds | One premium benefit remains while another source qualifies; show both management links, never sum durations. |
| Restore same account on a different platform versus new account with existing owner | Previously verified ownership follows the account; existing-owner conflict cannot transfer purchases or expose identity. |
| Deliberate deletion, two new accounts restore concurrently | One explicit verified reassignment; losing request sees a conflict, retries stay idempotent; no private data or allowance moves. |
| Provider customer already deleted, broad transfer scope, old Apple receipt history | Qualified re-ingestion respects the accepted exception without transferring unrelated subscriptions or charging an unusable purchase. |
| Old webhook or older in-flight verification after reassignment/deletion | No resurrection, rollback of ownership generation or stale entitlement overwrite. |
| Clock change, reboot uncertainty, delayed response or backup reinstall | No deadline extension from displayed time, receipt arrival or restored anchors; required revalidation preserves settlement/history. |
| Upgrade/downgrade mid training-bankroll turn or craps settlement | Finish/settle original funding exactly once; no premium winnings in free allowance and no new-day refill. |
| Missed webhooks, provider/store outage, exhausted retries or rate limits | Durable reconciliation/retry, unchanged cached deadlines, actionable pending state and alerts; no inferred revocation from transport failure. |
| Backup predates deletion or benefit restoration | Reconcile protected ownership/deletion facts before service resumes; do not revive accounts or refresh V from backup time. |
| Sandbox evidence, forged customer ID, replayed token, wrong app/product | No unauthorized production entitlement or cross-account data access. |

Provider deletion/restore, token extraction, replacement semantics, grace fields and direct-store checks require sandbox/device qualification before production billing. A failure reopens the implementation design; it does not silently remove an accepted feature. No production purchase, credential setup or store configuration is performed during this planning ticket.

### Evidence checked during this decision

- [RevenueCat pricing](https://www.revenuecat.com/pricing): current published free threshold and tracked-revenue charge; include provider charges in the backend operating envelope.
- [RevenueCat restore behavior](https://www.revenuecat.com/docs/projects/restore-behavior): keep-original-owner rules and receipt-wide effects need explicit account handling.
- [RevenueCat subscription management](https://www.revenuecat.com/docs/subscription-guidance/managing-subscriptions): replacement behavior, notification needs and store-management links.
- [Apple billing grace configuration](https://developer.apple.com/help/app-store-connect/manage-subscriptions/enable-billing-grace-period-for-auto-renewable-subscriptions): 16-day monthly/annual grace is configurable and must be tested before production enablement.
- [Google subscription configuration](https://support.google.com/googleplay/android-developer/answer/140504?hl=en): grace, account hold and optional pause settings.
- [Google subscription changes](https://developer.android.com/google/play/billing/subscriptions): same-subscription base-plan replacement constraints differ from deferred replacement across subscription products. Map the chosen player-facing billing behavior to supported SDK/store configuration, not an assumed interchangeable replacement enum.
- [RevenueCat customer model](https://www.revenuecat.com/docs/api-v1/customer-info-model): request timestamps and a preferred management URL are not store-check timestamps or a complete list of overlapping subscriptions.
- [RevenueCat grace handling](https://www.revenuecat.com/docs/subscription-guidance/how-grace-periods-work): explicit grace fields must be interpreted separately from billing issue/cancellation events.
- [RevenueCat webhook fields](https://www.revenuecat.com/docs/integrations/webhooks/event-types-and-fields): temporary entitlement grants are distinct from completed store validation.
- [Apple current subscription status workflow](https://developer.apple.com/videos/play/wwdc2022/10040/?time=657) and [Google subscription lifecycle](https://developer.android.com/google/play/billing/lifecycle/subscriptions): current-store endpoints support supplemental verification; the combined architecture is our accepted design, not a provider guarantee.
- [Google purchase security](https://developer.android.com/google/play/billing/security): backend verification, purchase token handling and timely acknowledgement.

These documents establish API/configuration facts, not evidence that True Count's implementation has passed the required scenarios.

23.title: Subscription verification and entitlement implementation

28.body:
## Question

What launch workload, operating-cost envelope and disaster-recovery policy should the selected backend support, and what evidence must validate them before release?

Establish monthly active players, active days and sessions, detail/history sizes and retention, concurrent connections, uploads, polling, notification/probe traffic, bulk downloads and authentication delivery assumptions. Count complete-stack costs for Supabase, Cloudflare Workers, Lambda, backups and related usage against the accepted initial $50/month backend target, separate from standardized-simulation compute. Use measured representative operations or an explicitly bounded feasibility investigation; label scenarios and estimates rather than presenting unmeasured traffic as forecasts. Include snapshot-creation cost/lock duration and large-result chunk handling.

Choose backup retention, independent copies, recovery-point and restoration-time objectives, restore ownership/runbook and validation. The suggested maximum one hour of lost server-acknowledged updates and restoration within 24 hours are PROVISIONAL: the user deferred disaster recovery while confirming it is required. They are not an accepted service guarantee. Supabase daily backups alone do not establish them, and selecting Supabase did not approve its approximately $130/month minimum configuration with point-in-time recovery. Recheck current first-party pricing and consider explicit budget/objective tradeoffs.

Recovery must reconcile grants and allowance-device ownership, command/result receipts, frozen transfers, deletion state, sharing withdrawal periods and public aggregates before service resumes. Restoring an older database must not duplicate allowance or payouts, republish withdrawn data, resurrect deleted accounts/records, or treat a stale entitlement as newly verified. Include object/provider configuration and control state that database backups omit, delayed devices, private staged uploads/snapshots, key/credential recovery and account-deletion obligations. State how recovery is exercised and what happens if the chosen guarantee cannot fit the target.

## Inputs and boundaries

- Part of [True Count — MVP decision map](https://github.com/0xRowdy/true-count/issues/1).
- Accepted provider and transaction contracts: [Local persistence and account synchronization architecture](https://github.com/0xRowdy/true-count/issues/21). Repository evidence: `docs/research/backend-provider-costs.md` and `docs/research/trusted-device-time.md`.
- Region and market inputs: [Launch markets and data residency](https://github.com/0xRowdy/true-count/issues/27).
- Account deletion/export/revocation: [Authentication and account lifecycle](https://github.com/0xRowdy/true-count/issues/22).
- Entitlement recovery: [Subscription verification and entitlement implementation](https://github.com/0xRowdy/true-count/issues/23).
- Keep the three-game scope, private casino records, existing histories and accepted native durability/recovery checks. Costs do not authorize silent scope cuts or weaker synchronization correctness.
- Planning only. Use grilling/domain-modeling and delegated primary-source research as needed. Do not provision paid infrastructure or operate a production restore while resolving this ticket.

## Resolution

Record accepted workload assumptions, complete cost model, limits/alerts and scaling triggers, backup/recovery objectives and procedure, restore acceptance scenarios, and explicit remaining implementation evidence. If a bounded benchmark is still needed, create a precise follow-up rather than claiming validation has already run.

## First planning round — accepted inputs

The user accepted the launch workload scenario: 1,000 monthly active players, each active 10 days/month with two 20-minute sessions per active day, plus a 5× growth scenario. These are planning/test assumptions, not a demand forecast or measured capacity. This implies 20,000 sessions and 400,000 session-minutes/month initially; the growth scenario is 100,000 sessions and 2,000,000 session-minutes. Additional foreground usage, concurrent peaks, traffic and record sizes remain to be sized.

Keep $50/month as the initial backend target, separate from standardized-simulation compute. The user wants low initial cost and permits reconsidering spending as users grow; no specific increase, purchase, or recovery-cost tradeoff is accepted yet.

The user confirmed they will be the primary outage responder with another person as backup. Responder availability, escalation timing and recovery objectives remain to be decided; this does not establish continuous coverage.

The ticket remains open. Backup architecture, retention, recovery objectives, complete-stack costs and release validation are still under review.

## Recovery direction and possible disposable beta — accepted inputs

The user accepted these eventual recovery objectives, applicable when recovery is implemented and validated:

- At most 24 hours of lost ordinary server-acknowledged history after a disaster. Existing protection against resurrected deletions/sharing withdrawals and duplicated ownership/allowance remains part of recovery correctness.
- Restoration within 24 hours of outage start.
- Three days of app-managed independent backup history, rather than the proposed seven days.

Supabase Pro currently includes seven days of provider-managed daily backups. Accepting that provider window alongside three-day independent copies has been proposed, but has not yet been explicitly confirmed. No three-day provider purge capability is established.

The user may run a soft/beta launch to collect feedback and then reset the servers; retaining that test data would not be required. Whether to use this phase and when to require the recovery system remain **TBD**. The user explicitly confirmed **sandbox subscriptions only** for such a beta. Do not interpret this as authorization to reset infrastructure or delete data now. Reset disclosure, exact cleanup/device behavior and transition to durable service still need a concrete release contract.

Saved player-history retention in durable service has not been shortened to three days. The three-day choice concerns backup history. No paid service has been purchased, backup implemented, restore tested or service guarantee established. The ticket remains open.

## Capacity, backup windows and exercise timing — accepted inputs

- The user accepted Supabase Pro's included seven-day provider backup window alongside three days of app-managed independent copies.
- The user accepted peak-capacity test assumptions of 100 simultaneously connected players initially and 500 in the 5× growth scenario, including sign-in/reconnection/history-download bursts. These are test scenarios, not measured capacity or player caps.
- Recovery exercises belong shortly after MVP, rather than being an MVP gate. The eventual 24-hour maximum ordinary-history loss and 24-hour restoration targets remain unverified until implementation and exercises establish them. The proposed ongoing quarterly/post-material-change exercise cadence has not yet been separately confirmed.

This preserves the possible disposable beta with sandbox-only subscriptions and its TBD activation/timing. It does not authorize a live reset or claim any recovery system is implemented. Exact follow-up scheduling and the transition to validated recovery remain to be specified. The ticket remains open.

## Backup sequencing, budget response and incident routing — accepted inputs

- **Independent backup provider:** Backblaze B2 in a US region is accepted for the planned independent copies. This functionality is explicitly **after MVP**; functionality comes first. Do not treat B2 provisioning, independent backups or their validation as an MVP gate. Three-day independent-copy retention remains the eventual design, alongside Supabase's included seven-day provider window.
- **Budget response:** alert at projected monthly backend spending of $40 against the initial $50 target. The team decides the response. The proposed automatic throttling is not accepted; an alert does not authorize throttling, service shutdown, deletion or an automatic spending increase.
- **Incident routing:** notify the standby agent first, then escalate to the user if the agent cannot resolve the incident within a 10-minute window. This supersedes the proposed user-first/30-minute escalation. Whether the standby agent is automated, its access/action scope and failure-to-acknowledge behavior still need clarification. No operational agent or alert integration has been deployed.

The user prioritizes MVP functionality. Recovery exercises and app-managed independent backups are post-MVP work; recovery objectives remain unverified until the relevant implementation and checks are complete. The possible disposable beta and its timing remain TBD. The ticket remains open.

## Automated first responder — confirmed

The user confirmed that the standby agent is an **automated AI operations agent** monitoring the operational items in this decision. It is the first responder, with escalation to the user if it cannot resolve an incident within the accepted ten-minute window.

The agent's permitted actions, deployment timing, independent failure detection, timer semantics and escalation channel are still to be specified. Confirmation of an automated agent does not itself accept the proposed predefined remediation set or authorize live infrastructure changes. Include agent hosting, model usage and alert delivery in the complete-stack cost model; do not assume these are free or included in Supabase/PostHog.

## Automated responder scope, sequence and delivery — accepted

The user accepted diagnosis and predefined remediation using available tools, for example obtaining PostHog logs and reporting findings or attempting a fix. The accepted proposed boundary permits predefined retries of idempotent jobs and restarts of stateless workers; database restores, data deletion, permission changes and spending increases require a human decision. Escalate immediately when that decision is required, rather than waiting out the ten-minute window.

The automated responder is **after all MVP functionality**. Escalation channels are **Email and Slack**. The proposed independent timeout/failure alert remains part of the implementation design to review; no actual integration or message delivery has been tested. This planning acceptance does not send messages, configure accounts or operate infrastructure now.

Model agent execution, hosting and delivery costs explicitly. Available tool access and least-privilege credentials must be qualified during implementation; do not assume PostHog application telemetry supplies every provider's infrastructure log. Preserve the prohibition on private histories/tokens in routine operational telemetry and model context.

## Cost investigation, temporary retention and exercise cadence — accepted

The user accepted:

- A provisional $10/month email reserve and a bounded workload/cost investigation covering history growth, large uploads/downloads, reconnect bursts and snapshot costs. The reserve is not a provider quote or proof the complete stack fits $50.
- Abandoned upload chunks expire after 24 hours without progress; routine operational logs retain 30 days; restricted incident/security evidence retains 90 days, subject to provider/privacy qualification. These do not shorten saved player histories.
- The first recovery exercise after implementation, then quarterly and after material recovery changes. These exercises remain after MVP functionality.

The consolidated working decision is `docs/decisions/backend-operating-envelope-disaster-recovery.md`. Remaining detailed proposals and scoped follow-ups will be reviewed before closing this ticket.

## Resolution — accepted operating envelope and post-MVP recovery

The user accepted Q1–Q18 and then confirmed the complete integrated operating plan with “Looks good.” This resolution is the canonical accepted planning contract. The repository mirror is `docs/decisions/backend-operating-envelope-disaster-recovery.md`. This is not provisioned infrastructure, measured capacity, verified recovery or approval to deploy/reset servers. Explicitly identified follow-ups remain separate decisions and investigations.

## Accepted scope and sequence

- Preserve Supabase in Virginia, global Cloudflare probe, direct Lambda probe in Oregon, PostHog US Cloud, existing account/synchronization/entitlement contracts and the three-game scope.
- Initial backend target: $50/month, separate from standardized-simulation compute. Keep initial costs low; reconsider spending as users grow. Alert at $40 projected monthly spend. The team decides the response; no automatic throttling, deletion, service shutdown or spending increase follows from an alert.
- Functionality first. App-managed independent backups, recovery exercises and the automated operations responder follow MVP functionality. Their eventual targets are not MVP release gates or demonstrated guarantees.
- A disposable soft/beta launch with a later server reset is possible, not decided. Such a beta uses sandbox subscriptions only. Its exact timing and transition to durable service remain TBD; no reset is authorized now. This does not shorten saved history retention in durable service.
- Eventual recovery targets: at most 24 hours of ordinary server-acknowledged history lost, and restoration within 24 hours of outage start. Protect deletion/withdrawal/ownership correctness; data loss cannot authorize resurrection or duplicate allowances.
- Supabase's included provider backups retain seven days. Planned independent copies use Backblaze B2 in a US region and retain three days.
- Human response coverage: the user with another person as backup. Planned automated first response precedes escalation to the user after ten minutes unresolved, through Email and Slack.
- The automated agent may inspect available tools/logs, including PostHog, report findings, and attempt predefined fixes such as an idempotent job retry or stateless-worker restart. Database restores, data deletion, permission changes and spending increases require human decision; escalate immediately when that decision is needed. No deployed tool integration or remediation is claimed.

## Accepted workload scenarios

| Input | Initial scenario | Growth scenario |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Monthly active players | 1,000 | 5,000 |
| Active days/player/month | 10 | 10 |
| Sessions/active day | 2 | 2 |
| Session duration | 20 minutes | 20 minutes |
| Sessions/month | 20,000 | 100,000 |
| Foreground session-minutes/month | 400,000 | 2,000,000 |
| Peak simultaneously connected players | 100 | 500 |

These are planning and test assumptions, not demand forecasts, player caps or proven throughput. Non-session foreground time, multiple devices and background/provider traffic add to this baseline.

## Workload accounting and authorized bounded qualification

Use the accepted 60-second foreground reconciliation and 30-second eligible-activity probe cadence. Base reconciliation counts are roughly 400,000 / 2,000,000 monthly, plus opening/reconnection, changes, retries and non-session use. If every session-minute needed probing, primary probes would be 800,000 / 4,000,000, plus entry checks. Normal fallback Lambda traffic depends on primary failures; also test all-primary-failed conditions so fallback is not assumed free. Count provider checks separately: six-hour-stale foreground refresh, at least daily active/grace/retrying/held subscription reconciliation, boundary checks and event/restore/purchase traffic. Never poll stores per gameplay turn or every account reconciliation.

Model two connected devices per active account as an additional stress case. Count connections rather than equating players with connections. Realtime notifications carry change hints, not private record bodies. Account for fan-out, notification-triggered fetches, repeated downloads and bootstrap restart costs.

Use result-payload sensitivity cases of 10 KB, 100 KB and 1 MB per completed session, then replace these assumptions with representative serialized artifacts. They imply about 0.2 / 2 / 20 GB of raw new payload per initial month, or 1 / 10 / 100 GB at growth volume, before indexes, receipts, feed entries, database overhead, backup copies and deletion. This is cost sensitivity, not permission to retain only small records or to cap player histories. Preserve existing on-demand old detail and Download all history.

For qualification, use 1-year and 5-year histories, plus a heavy account with 100,000 summaries. Exercise a 10 MB chunked result and the eventual maximum supported result, partial uploads, late retries, interrupted downloads, concurrent summary-snapshot creation, deletion and account changes. Measure snapshot lock duration separately from total creation/download time; the accepted consistent-watermark contract cannot be traded away for speed. Add bootstrap/export bursts affecting 10% of active accounts, and outage reconnection bursts at the accepted peaks.

Provisional supporting traffic assumptions: 10% subscribing accounts; two transactional emails per MAU/month; ten analytics events per completed session plus bounded aggregate operational events; a 20% request/retry allowance, with explicit failure-storm tests beyond that allowance. These are cost inputs only, not product limits, a subscriber forecast or a provider selection. Include sign-in, recovery/linking, deletion completion, delivery retries and incident emails, then reconcile the email service decision before production use.

The authorized [Backend workload and cost feasibility](https://github.com/0xRowdy/true-count/issues/37) investigation must implement representative operations against a synthetic dataset and report database size, query/transaction timings, snapshot lock duration, CPU/memory, API/function/message counts, compressed upload/download/backup bytes, nationwide latency and extrapolated monthly costs at both scenarios. Include authentication, grants/transfers, privacy withdrawal, staged chunks, snapshots, exports and deletion, current-store verification mocks plus documented provider qualification, and simultaneous reconnects. It must not claim production validation from quota arithmetic. Prefer local/offline measurement first; paid cloud runs require separately authorized access/spending. Return a priced gap if $50 is infeasible; never silently cut histories, games or correctness.

## Current cost inputs — evidence, not an accepted bill

Verified official sources on 2026-09-07. USD list prices before taxes; credits/free allowances may be shared with other workloads.

| Component | Cost input and accounting boundary |
| --- | --- |
| Supabase Pro | $25/month baseline; includes one Micro via compute credit, 100,000 Auth MAU, 8 GB database disk, 100 GB file storage, 2 million Edge Function calls, 500 peak Realtime connections and 5 million Realtime messages. More compute may be needed regardless of quota headroom. |
| Supabase usage | Uncached egress includes 250 GB, then $0.09/GB; cached egress has a separate allowance/rate and cannot be substituted for private uncached traffic. Realtime excess connections round up in 1,000-connection packages at $10; message excess rounds in 1-million packages at $2.50. Multiple devices can exceed included connection capacity at the 500-player scenario. |
| Cloudflare Workers | Paid $5/month: 10 million requests and 30 million CPU-ms included; excess $0.30/million requests and $0.02/million CPU-ms. No selection of a native database-dump executor is implied. |
| Lambda probe | Oregon x86 requests $0.20/million and first-tier compute $0.0000166667/GB-second. Deduct only remaining shared 1-million-request / 400,000-GB-second free allowance. Function URL adds no endpoint charge. Add logging and transfer; AWS free internet transfer is shared across services/regions. |
| PostHog | Analytics first 1 million events/month free, then starting $0.00005/event; error tracking first 100,000 exceptions free, then starting $0.00037/exception. Avoid per-turn/minute success events when aggregates answer the question. Private records and secrets stay out of telemetry. |
| RevenueCat | Free below $2,500 monthly tracked revenue; at the threshold, 1% of all tracked revenue. Include in the backend/service model, separate from app-store commissions. This can materially consume headroom as subscriptions grow. |
| Email / Slack delivery | Production email provider remains its existing decision. The user accepted a provisional $10/month reserve for email/delivery in the initial scenario, not a quoted provider price or sufficient-volume claim. Qualify Slack access, plan needs and delivery failure behavior. |
| Independent backups — post-MVP | B2 storage $6.95/TB/30-day with first 10 GB free. Include export executor, compression, database source transfer, object operations, retained versions, restore traffic and monitoring. A zero storage bill does not make backup operation free. |
| Automated responder — post-MVP | Model/agent hosting, execution, tool access and independent escalation are unpriced pending implementation choice. Do not hide these costs inside a free analytics quota. |

The initial fixed platform subtotal is $30 (Supabase + Workers), leaving $20 for all other charges. The accepted provisional $10 email reserve leaves $10 of planning headroom, not a verified all-in $50 bill. Track each component and projected month-end total. Simulation compute is accounted separately; shared infrastructure costs must be attributed once.

Illustrative dump sensitivity: one compressed 1 GB full export daily is roughly 30 GB/month of source transfer and roughly 3 GB for three independent daily copies. Actual retained versions and lifecycle timing may increase bytes. Full hourly exports would instead approach 730 GB/month, exceeding Supabase's uncached allowance by 480 GB before other traffic and adding $43.20. The daily-history objective avoids assuming hourly full dumps are affordable, but daily scheduling alone does not prove a hard 24-hour recovery point.

Sources: [Supabase pricing](https://supabase.com/pricing), [egress](https://supabase.com/docs/guides/platform/manage-your-usage/egress), [Realtime connections](https://supabase.com/docs/guides/platform/manage-your-usage/realtime-peak-connections), [messages](https://supabase.com/docs/guides/platform/manage-your-usage/realtime-messages), [Workers pricing](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/platform/pricing/), [Lambda pricing](https://aws.amazon.com/lambda/pricing/), [Oregon rates](https://pricing.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/offers/v1.0/aws/AWSLambda/current/us-west-2/index.json), [Function URLs](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/apig-http-invoke-decision.html), [AWS transfer allowance](https://aws.amazon.com/about-aws/global-infrastructure/global-network/faqs/), [PostHog analytics](https://posthog.com/product-analytics), [error tracking](https://posthog.com/error-tracking), [RevenueCat](https://www.revenuecat.com/pricing), [B2 pricing](https://www.backblaze.com/cloud-storage/pricing).

## Retention: accepted periods and remaining control schedule

Existing saved-history behavior is preserved: three-day backup retention does not erase three-day-old sessions. Active-system account deletion remains immediate access/public suppression with cleanup targeted within seven days; generated exports and temporary bootstrap snapshots expire after 24 hours.

Accepted additional periods (Q17), subject to provider/privacy qualification:

- Abandoned private upload chunks expire after 24 hours without progress; a returning client restarts staging from its retained local source. An incomplete upload never counts as an accepted result. Apply account-deletion cleanup sooner when required.
- Routine app-managed operational logs: 30 days. Security/incident evidence: 90 days, restricted to the minimum relevant metadata and operational access. Provider-managed retention is separately inventoried and qualified; do not claim these settings configure every provider. Actual legal holds need an explicit scope, owner, review and expiry, not indefinite blanket retention.

Accepted control-retention handoff:

- Independently protected deletion/revocation/withdrawal controls: do not select an arbitrary period before qualifying all recoverable backups and credential/replay paths. [Billing and recovery-control retention evidence](https://github.com/0xRowdy/true-count/issues/38) supplies the finite schedule to the privacy release decision. If a path prevents finite compaction, fix that path or explicitly revisit retention instead of silently keeping private history. Missing/deleted account IDs remain denied, and IDs are never reused.
- Receipts/feed compaction: use a protocol watermark and snapshot reset, not an age-only delete. A stale operation must become a safe retry/reconciliation or be rejected; it must never be treated as a fresh allowance, payout, privacy or ownership operation. Purge payloads once the accepted operation is durably represented and safe compaction is established. Finite age and maximum retained bytes need qualification with the workload investigation.
- Billing ownership/control retention and any legally necessary records use the same [focused evidence follow-up](https://github.com/0xRowdy/true-count/issues/38), with final policy choices owned by [US launch privacy rights and release disclosures](https://github.com/0xRowdy/true-count/issues/36). Do not invent a statutory retention period or discard evidence while a source can still confer benefits. This is a precise remaining decision, separate from retention of unrelated private history.

The operations owner maintains a table of category, purpose, storage/provider location, access, expiry trigger, cleanup job and failure alert. Include staged uploads, snapshots, exports, Auth/storage/provider copies and raw tokens; maintain the existing deletion ordering and provider revocation requirements. Provider backup/log geography and exact purge behavior remain qualification tasks under the accepted US-primary/disclosed-wider-processing contract.

## Accepted post-MVP recovery procedure

Choose B2 US West for independently controlled, encrypted backups, with separate restricted writer/restore credentials and separately recoverable encryption keys. The exact executor, schedule margin and immutability/lifecycle settings require the bounded recovery design and exercise; provider daily snapshots plus a cron schedule are not evidence of a maximum 24-hour loss. Protect database contents, Storage object bytes and versions needed for recovery, schema/migrations/pinned execution definitions, essential provider configuration and credential/key recovery references. Never dump secrets into source control or operational model context.

A human authorizes a restore. Fence affected writes, public reads and caches; preserve evidence and select the latest complete verified recovery set. Restore into an isolated environment, then reconcile independently protected control state and uncertain operations before reopening service. A database backup alone cannot preserve post-backup deletion, sharing withdrawals, device revocations, grant/transfer outcomes or accepted purchase ownership.

The control-recovery design must establish how sensitive acceptance is durably protected before it can be reported successful, and how partial cross-provider outcomes are resolved. It must fail closed on uncertain grants/transfers, sharing, deletion and purchase ownership; no distributed atomicity is assumed. Recover current store evidence without advancing verification time merely because a backup was loaded. Rebuild affected public aggregates only after withdrawal/deletion filtering. Invalidate stale server sessions or credentials where needed without extending device offline deadlines.

On delayed-device return, reconcile the server generation, local pending receipts and original allocation/expiry. No stale upload creates an account; no retry reapplies a payout; a frozen source transfer stays frozen until authoritative resolution. Client copies may recover ordinary histories only through accepted revision/conflict rules, never overriding protected deletions or fabricating lost results.

Before declaring recovery operational, exercise backup age, complete recovery duration, corrupted/missing copies, unavailable keys/provider, expired chunks/snapshots, a backup predating deletion/withdrawal/transfer/benefits-only restoration, delayed devices, competing restores and late webhooks. Verify no privacy resurrection, duplicated benefits/allowance/payouts or stale verified-at timestamp. The accepted repeat cadence is quarterly and after material changes, beginning after MVP functionality. If safety cannot be established, keep affected service fenced and escalate rather than reopening to meet the time target.

[Supabase backups](https://supabase.com/docs/guides/platform/backups) exclude Storage object bytes and custom-role passwords; deleting a project removes provider backups. [CLI export/restore](https://supabase.com/docs/guides/platform/migrating-within-supabase/backup-restore) is a starting point, not a complete runbook. [B2 regions](https://www.backblaze.com/docs/cloud-storage-data-regions) and [Object Lock](https://www.backblaze.com/docs/cloud-storage-object-lock) support the provider investigation; immutability duration must agree with finite retention and deletion disclosures.

## Accepted monitoring and responder design

Monitor availability, sync/transaction failures and queue age, snapshot lock/latency, storage/transfer growth, exports/deletion completion, subscription reconciliation and verification failures, security/access failures and projected spend. Preserve accepted webhook start-within-one-minute / alert-after-five-minute targets and Google acknowledgement alert at one hour. Later add backup age/validation failures and the automated responder's own health and spend.

Keep PostHog as the operational dashboard/telemetry tool. The agent can query other existing authorized provider tools when PostHog lacks needed evidence. Redact logs and treat their contents as untrusted data; a log line cannot authorize tool actions. Use a predefined action allowlist, per-incident attempt limits, identity-bound audit results and least-privilege access. Do not grant broad infrastructure access simply because a connector exists.

Start the ten-minute escalation deadline at initial alert dispatch, not when the agent begins working; retries do not reset it. Immediate human escalation covers missing authority, dangerous/ambiguous state, unavailable tools or a suspected privacy/security incident. Independent deterministic timeout/heartbeat delivery must alert through Email and Slack if the agent fails, stalls or cannot prove recovery. Preserve an incident ID to deduplicate while recording channel failures. Recovery means a fresh health check and relevant state checks pass, not merely that a restart command succeeded.

Before the automated responder is implemented: essential actionable alerts go directly to the human team; budget responses stay human-decided. Exact inbox, Slack channel, account credentials and named backup responder are implementation configuration, not secrets to place in this document. The production email decision must include operational escalation traffic. Agent implementation and periodic exercises follow MVP functionality; implementation is not claimed by this planning decision.

## Remaining decisions and handoffs

- [Backend workload and cost feasibility](https://github.com/0xRowdy/true-count/issues/37) owns the bounded measurements; they are not claimed to have happened.
- [Billing and recovery-control retention evidence](https://github.com/0xRowdy/true-count/issues/38) owns finite billing/ownership/receipt retention evidence and provider purge qualification; the privacy release decision consumes the answer and accepts the final schedule.
- [Disposable beta and durable-service transition](https://github.com/0xRowdy/true-count/issues/39) owns reset disclosure, server/device/provider cleanup, sandbox-to-production isolation and activation of durable service. The choice remains TBD, rather than automatically blocking MVP on independent backups or restores.
- Keep implementation of independent backups and the AI responder after MVP functionality. Their engineering tasks belong to delivery planning, not an implicit production implementation during this map session.

## Question

Which production email provider and delivery configuration should serve the accepted emailed sign-in codes and account messages, and what operating/privacy contract must it satisfy?

Choose the provider, sender/domain setup, required message types, delivery/retry and abuse limits, bounce/suppression handling, Apple private-relay compatibility, observability, and cost assumptions. Specify processing locations (including support/subprocessors), message/log retention, and deletion handling without treating the recipient mailbox as controlled by True Count. Preserve the existing Apple/Google/email-code account lifecycle and seven-day active-system deletion target, with finite justified exceptions.

## Inputs and boundaries

- Part of [True Count — MVP decision map](https://github.com/0xRowdy/true-count/issues/1).
- [Authentication and account lifecycle](https://github.com/0xRowdy/true-count/issues/22) selects email codes; [Launch markets and data residency](https://github.com/0xRowdy/true-count/issues/27) selects a Colorado publisher, US/English launch and US-primary hosting with disclosed wider processing.
- Supabase's default SMTP service is for testing and does not settle production delivery. Evidence: [Supabase custom SMTP](https://supabase.com/docs/guides/auth/auth-smtp).
- Feed costs and finite retention into [Backend operating envelope and disaster recovery](https://github.com/0xRowdy/true-count/issues/28). Its initial estimates may reserve an explicit email allowance; reconcile the chosen service before launch.
- Use grilling/domain-modeling and focused research. Planning only: no domain changes, provider signup or real email sends.

## Resolution

Record the accepted provider and delivery/privacy contract, cost inputs and exact configuration/release checks. Confirm the choice against the accepted account flows and budget; do not claim deliverability has been tested.
