## Accepted operations inputs

[Backend operating envelope and disaster recovery](https://github.com/0xRowdy/true-count/issues/28) has accepted a **provisional $10/month email reserve** within the initial $50 backend target. This is not a provider price or a sufficient-capacity finding. Reconcile the selected email service's costs and message volume with that model.

Operational escalation must support **Email and Slack**. The planned automated AI responder follows all MVP functionality, uses existing authorized tools/logs and predefined fixes, and escalates unresolved incidents to the user after ten minutes, immediately if a human decision is required. Include the operational email type, sender/delivery/retry constraints and channel-failure handling in this decision. No email, Slack message or configuration is sent by this handoff.

The operating decision's consolidated review remains pending; these particular inputs were explicitly accepted in the live session.

[Backend operating envelope and disaster recovery](https://github.com/0xRowdy/true-count/issues/28#issuecomment-5573796177) is now resolved. The complete integrated plan accepts direct essential alerts to the human team before the post-MVP AI responder exists, Email and Slack escalation, the provisional $10/month email reserve, and illustrative two transactional messages per MAU/month for the workload investigation. Include incident, account-lifecycle and sign-in traffic and reconcile actual provider costs/volume; these assumptions are not provider prices or delivery limits. Agent retries do not restart its eventual ten-minute escalation deadline, and independent timeout delivery must cover agent failure. No alert integration has been deployed.

## Resolution — accepted email provider and delivery operations

Accepted through live discussion (Q1–Q8). This is an accepted planning contract, not a provisioned account, DNS configuration or a sent production email.

### Accepted choices

- **Provider and tier:** Resend, starting on the **free tier** ($0/month). Most users are expected to sign in through Apple/Google rather than email codes, so real volume should land well under the free tier's 3,000/month (100/day) cap even at initial launch scale. Revisit tier (Pro, $20/month for 50,000 emails) only if usage approaches the cap or the growth scenario (5,000 MAU) — not as a day-one commitment. This is consistent with the backend operating envelope's ["reconsider spending as users grow"](https://github.com/0xRowdy/true-count/issues/28#issuecomment-5573796177) posture, and comes in at $0 rather than the $10 provisional email reserve, so no budget conflict at launch.
- **Required message types:** sign-in one-time codes; security alerts (device revocation, new sign-in method linked); deletion confirmation; data-export-ready notice; operational incident-escalation mail to the response team. No marketing/newsletter mail at launch.
- **Abuse limits:** app-level per-account and per-IP rate limits on code requests (a handful per hour with backoff), enforced ahead of and tighter than Supabase's own adjustable SMTP rate cap.
- **Delivery/retry:** fail synchronously back to the requesting client on send failure; no background retry queue. A delayed code arriving after a retry queue drains is close to useless given codes are already short-lived. Keep it to the bare minimum for MVP. Repeated failures feed observability rather than being silently retried.
- **Bounce/suppression:** rely on Resend's automatic suppression list — hard bounces and spam complaints are suppressed account-wide across domains without a custom bounce-handling pipeline.
- **Retention/content:** True Count stores no independent copy of message bodies, only that a message of a given type was sent (consistent with the existing prohibition on logging email codes or provider tokens). Resend's own retention is fixed at 30 days on every plan, matching the general 30-day operational-log period already accepted for the backend. No proactive purge from Resend is needed on account deletion, since True Count holds no independent copy and does not control the recipient's mailbox.
- **Apple private-relay compatibility:** register both the primary sending domain and Resend's `send.` subdomain as Apple email sources (Resend's return-path uses a subdomain, so both must be registered); Resend enforces SPF/DKIM by default, satisfying Apple's authentication requirement once domains are registered.
- **Processing location:** Resend's privacy policy states data is processed in the United States, consistent with the accepted US-primary/disclosed-wider-processing residency model from [Launch markets and data residency](https://github.com/0xRowdy/true-count/issues/27). Exact infrastructure/subprocessor regions are not published beyond "United States."
- **Observability:** delivery failure rate, bounce/complaint rate, and send-queue age as aggregate PostHog metrics only — never message bodies or recipient addresses in analytics payloads.

### Evidence

Checked 2026-09-08 against primary and current sources.

- [Supabase custom SMTP guide](https://supabase.com/docs/guides/auth/auth-smtp): default SMTP is not production-ready (2 msg/hour, no SLA); lists Resend, AWS SES, Postmark, SendGrid, ZeptoMail, Brevo as supported.
- [Resend pricing](https://resend.com/pricing): free tier 3,000 emails/month capped at 100/day; Pro $20/month for 50,000.
- [AWS SES pricing](https://aws.amazon.com/ses/pricing/), [SES production access](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/ses/latest/dg/request-production-access.html), [SES account-level suppression](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/ses/latest/dg/sending-email-suppression-list.html): considered and rejected in favor of Resend's lower operational overhead, despite materially lower cost (~$0.10/1,000 emails).
- [Postmark pricing](https://postmarkapp.com/pricing): considered and rejected — cheapest plan ($15/month for 10,000 emails) exceeds the $10 provisional reserve immediately.
- [Resend suppression list](https://resend.com/changelog/suppression-list-support): automatic account-wide suppression on hard bounce/complaint.
- Resend data retention: fixed 30 days on all plans (raised from a shorter window in March 2026, per current provider documentation).
- [Resend Apple private relay guide](https://resend.com/docs/knowledge-base/sending-apple-private-relay): domain + subdomain registration steps, automatic SPF/DKIM.
- [Resend privacy policy](https://resend.com/legal/privacy-policy): US data processing; subprocessor detail deferred to Resend's subprocessors page.
- [Apple private email relay authentication requirements](https://www.suped.com/learn/dmarc/what-are-apples-requirements-for-email-authentication-and-domain-registration): domain registration in Apple Developer, SPF/DKIM alignment required or mail bounces.

### Open follow-up (not blocking this ticket)

No production domain exists yet. Domain selection/purchase is a prerequisite **operational** task before DKIM/SPF and Apple-relay registration can actually happen — this is implementation, not a further planning decision, so it does not get its own map ticket per this map's planning-only scope. Flag it for the delivery/release effort that follows this map.

### Named handoffs

- [Backend operating envelope and disaster recovery](https://github.com/0xRowdy/true-count/issues/28): the $10 provisional email reserve is unaffected at launch ($0 actual); reconcile if/when Resend's Pro tier becomes necessary.
- [US launch privacy rights and release disclosures](https://github.com/0xRowdy/true-count/issues/36): consumes this provider's processing-location and retention facts for the final disclosure contract.

Planning only: no domain was purchased, no Resend account was created, and no email was sent during this session.

## Question

Can representative implementations of the accepted backend operations support the agreed launch and growth scenarios within the initial $50/month backend target, and what measured limit or priced change is required if not?

Part of [True Count — MVP decision map](https://github.com/0xRowdy/true-count/issues/1). Follow-up authorized in [Backend operating envelope and disaster recovery](https://github.com/0xRowdy/true-count/issues/28). Planning feasibility only: build a throwaway representative harness, not the production app. No paid provisioning is authorized by this ticket.

## Fixed inputs

- Launch: 1,000 MAU, 10 active days/month, two 20-minute sessions per active day: 20,000 sessions and 400,000 foreground minutes/month; 100 simultaneously connected players.
- Growth: 5× monthly workload; 500 simultaneous players. Also measure multiple-device connection overhead.
- Supabase Virginia; Workers primary probe and Lambda Oregon fallback; PostHog US; existing 60-second account reconciliation and 30-second eligible-activity probe cadence. Preserve atomic receipts/account changes, privacy ordering, grants/transfers and consistent snapshot watermarks from [Local persistence and account synchronization architecture](https://github.com/0xRowdy/true-count/issues/21).
- $50 initial target, separate from simulation compute; alert at $40 projected spend and let the team decide. $10 email reserve is provisional pending [Transactional email provider and delivery operations](https://github.com/0xRowdy/true-count/issues/33).
- B2 independent backups, restore exercises and AI operations automation are AFTER MVP functionality. Model their incremental costs separately; do not make their execution an MVP gate.

## Bounded investigation

One research session: a documented local Postgres/Supabase-compatible harness with synthetic data and a small representative transaction/API set, plus current first-party price/limit checks. Include accepted result+receipt/feed updates; allowance grant/transfer concurrency; sharing withdrawal/contribution races; coherent summary snapshot creation; staged upload/chunk completion; resumable bootstrap/export; deletion cleanup. Stub third-party billing/email calls with their documented invocation cadence and report those boundaries honestly. Do not pretend a stub qualifies a provider integration.

Sweep 10 KB/100 KB/1 MB result payloads; 1-year/5-year histories and one 100,000-summary account; a 10 MB chunked result plus any actual supported maximum established by the harness. Test 100/500 connected-client equivalents, reconnect/download bursts, repeated retry and aborted staging. Report snapshot lock duration independently from total time, peak memory, storage/index/feed/receipt growth, message fan-out, calls, serialized/compressed bytes and upload/download completion.

Use 10% subscribing accounts, two transactional messages/MAU/month, ten analytics events/session and 20% routine retry traffic as explicitly illustrative sensitivity inputs, not product limits. Include auth/provider boundary events, webhook queues, polling, notification fetches, both probes during failure, current-store checks, export expiry and seven-day account cleanup work. Add 10% simultaneous-account bootstrap/export stress. Replace assumptions where measurements provide better evidence.

Reprice complete-stack usage: Supabase compute/database/API/Realtime/storage/egress, Workers, Lambda/logging/transfer, PostHog, RevenueCat, email/delivery reserve, and separate post-MVP backup executor/storage/transfer and AI-agent costs. Do not double count simulation compute or assume free allowances are exclusive. Report unknown AI/provider costs explicitly.

## Answer and stopping rule

Publish a reproducible Markdown report and linked harness/results with exact environment, commands, versions, assumptions, operation definitions and cost arithmetic. Separate local timings from cloud throughput/nationwide latency; qualify any cloud evidence only with separately available authorized access. Stop after the bounded sweep with a list of remaining implementation checks, rather than expanding into a production backend.

Return measured pass/gap evidence and proposed limits or budget changes. Never declare $50 feasible solely because MAU fits a free quota; never delete history, weaken correctness or reduce the three-game scope to make the model fit.
